evidence_class: RANKED UNTRIED FAULT-ZONE-ANATOMY HYPOTHESES — qualitative priorities, not scores
status: RESEARCH SHORTLIST ONLY; NOT IMPLEMENTED OR RUN; three-experiment/two-hour budget spent
novelty_scope: Compared with the inspected fault-zone-anatomy implementations and experiments recorded in this repository; no claim of global novelty.
ranking_basis: Risk-adjusted, qualitative prior on relative incremental DTI potential, implementation cost, and data readiness. These are not numeric scores or forecasts; confidence is low. The latest stored holdout is not reproducible under the current evaluator hash and the literal registry gate blocks any nonempty candidate, so no idea is actionable now.
current_blocker: A separately SHA-verified raster in the 679-entry inventory covers every allowable candidate cell under the 3-pixel overlap test. Under the unchanged literal >70% rule, the gate is unsatisfiable for any nonempty candidate while the witness remains in scope; do not change the threshold or test these ideas without renewed owner authorization.

candidates.hypothesis: Segment-pair stepover and bend geometry predicts connector, tip, or subparallel secondary strands.
layers: Visible existing-fault raster and pinned trace-segment vectors
Gap width, overlap, segment endpoints, and host orientation
Recorded sense only when a reliable visible-only join supports a releasing/restraining classification
candidates.physical_signature: Predeclared geometric classes for narrow-gap connectors versus wider-step tip/subparallel zones; no hard-coded textbook shear angle.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: Short linking or subparallel strands may occur between or beside mapped host segments rather than on an existing catalogue trace.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: Tests a segment-pair geometry rule with distinct connector/tip outcomes, not the tested nearest-host distance/offset/length baseline, candidate magnetic-edge strike, or sense-only ablation. Detailed endpoint and gap definitions must be frozen before any future holdout evaluation.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Alluvial-fan risers, drainage lineaments, magnetic/lithologic contacts, or map generalization can align near fault segments.
candidates.qualitative_priority: Highest of this shortlist; expected DTI effect unknown.
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; vector pairing and leakage-safe visible-only geometry need tests.
candidates.data_readiness: Local trace vectors are present; provenance and host-sense missingness still require audit.

sources.citation: Wang et al. (2017), Strain partitioning and stress perturbation around stepovers and bends of strike-slip faults: Numerical results, Tectonophysics 721, 211–226.
sources.checked_takeaway: Models show stress/strain localization around bends and stepovers; narrow and wider steps can localize deformation differently. Mechanism support only, not a DTI claim.

sources.citation: Zhu et al. (2024), An overview of structures associated with bends of strike-slip faults, Marine and Petroleum Geology 167, 106983.
sources.checked_takeaway: Structures vary with angle, displacement, stress regime, and analogue/numerical setup; no universal bend rule is assumed.

candidates.future_test_gate: Only after renewed authorization: preregister visible-only pair rules, then whole-segment hide-and-recover, pixel-exact masking, pooled DTI, canary, and registry checks.

relative_expected_dti_upside.reason: Directly targets connectors and tip/subparallel strands that a radial halo may miss; effect on the competition DTI is unknown.

candidates.hypothesis: Fault-tip relay and termination anatomy differs from the mid-fault damage-zone wall and predicts some missed secondary strands.
layers: Visible fault raster and vector endpoints
Signed along-strike tip distance and neighboring-segment linkage
candidates.physical_signature: Matched tip-neighborhood versus mid-wall recovery, evaluated on both sides and with relay/linkage kept distinct from termination.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: Some secondary strands may form relay/link structures near segment ends, while other tips may be barriers or growth-arrest zones.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: Tests signed endpoint-relative position and segment linkage rather than unsigned nearest-fault distance, an isotropic halo, or the previously tested candidate-strike term.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Alluvial-fan margins, dry washes, road corridors, and mapped trace truncation can create apparent tip lineaments.
candidates.implementation_cost: Low to medium; careful vector endpoint matching and matched controls required.
candidates.data_readiness: Existing vector trace endpoints are present; no new raster is required.

sources.citation: d’Alessio & Martel (2004), Fault terminations and barriers to fault growth, Journal of Structural Geology 26, 1885–1896.
sources.checked_takeaway: Small faults near a major fault-system tip can diffuse stress and inhibit growth; tip enrichment is not assumed to be universally beneficial.
Wider stepovers can localize strain near segment tips in the modeled settings; this motivates a bidirectional test, not a gain prediction.

candidates.future_test_gate: Hide whole components and compare tip versus matched mid-wall held-out positives without truth-informed endpoint definitions; reject leakage or unstable tip-class results.

relative_expected_dti_upside.reason: Tip-localized secondary strands are plausible but may cover few withheld pixels and are sensitive to mapped endpoint quality.

candidates.hypothesis: A defensible host-maturity or displacement-related covariate changes secondary-strand density and damage-zone decay beyond the current host-length proxy.
layers: Visible trace geometry and component length
Independently recorded host attributes, only after a documented join and missingness audit
candidates.physical_signature: An empirically estimated change in radial strand density/decay with host maturity or cumulative displacement; present-day slip rate is not silently substituted for cumulative displacement.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: Damage-zone width and secondary-fracture distribution can evolve with host displacement, so reliable maturity metadata could distinguish where strands are likely beyond a simple length proxy.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: Adds one independently justified host covariate to the tested length-based anatomy; it does not treat fault length or slip rate as measured displacement.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Inherited joints, lithologic contacts, mapping intensity, and catalogue attribute-boundary errors.
candidates.qualitative_priority: Third; expected DTI effect unknown and data-dependent.
candidates.implementation_cost: Low to medium if a reliable attribute join exists; otherwise data-blocked.
candidates.data_readiness: Local attribute tables exist, but host-level coverage, join precision, and cumulative-displacement availability have not been established.

sources.citation: Savage & Brodsky (2011), Collateral damage: Evolution with displacement of fracture distribution and secondary fault strands in fault damage zones, JGR: Solid Earth 116, B03405.
sources.checked_takeaway: Observed fracture/secondary-strand patterns relate to displacement; this does not justify replacing cumulative displacement with fault length or present-day slip rate.

candidates.future_test_gate: First inspect joins and missingness without holdout outcomes; only a prespecified independently supported covariate may enter a later spatial holdout.

relative_expected_dti_upside.reason: An independent maturity covariate could refine the existing length proxy, but available attributes may be redundant, missing, or biased.

candidates.hypothesis: Independent geophysical contrast inside a fixed visible-fault damage-zone halo can corroborate some secondary strands beyond geometry alone.
layers: A fixed halo from visible-only mapped fault geometry
Magnetic-gradient magnitude/coherence or other officially documented local geophysical bands
candidates.physical_signature: Local edge/gradient support within a preregistered halo; this is not an unconstrained survey-wide geophysical classifier and is distinct from the already-tested candidate magnetic-edge relative-strike feature.
candidates.why_it_may_find_missing_faults: A strand without a catalogue trace may still offset or juxtapose magnetized units, producing a local geophysical contrast near an existing fault zone.
candidates.difference_from_inspected_work: Tests within-halo scalar corroboration, not the previously tested candidate magnetic-edge tangent/orientation interaction.
candidates.named_non_fault_mimic: Magnetic lithologic contacts, surficial drainage, cultural metal, and flight-line leveling artifacts.
candidates.implementation_cost: High because exact file coverage, CRS, band meaning, and registration must be verified first.
candidates.data_readiness: Data-blocked. The competition feature stack is absent. GDR submission 1591 displays public access and CC BY 4.0, while the linked USGS/ScienceBase record is separately recorded as CC0 1.0 in the source audit. No exact binary asset/license receipt, usable file, AOI coverage, band definitions, CRS or grid alignment has been verified; do not treat this source as an obtainable usable feature yet.

sources.citation: Grauch (2002), High-resolution aeromagnetic survey to image shallow faults, Dixie Valley geothermal field, Nevada, USGS Open-File Report 2002-384.
sources.checked_takeaway: Official report record documents an aeromagnetic shallow-fault imaging analogue; it does not establish coverage or alignment with the contest grid.

sources.citation: Glen & Earney (2024), GeoDAWN airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys of the northwestern Great Basin, GDR submission 1591 / USGS ScienceBase DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ.
sources.checked_takeaway: GDR submission 1591 displays public access and CC BY 4.0 and links to USGS ScienceBase, whose separate record is marked CC0 1.0 in the source audit. Exact binary asset/license, spatial overlap, usable files, CRS and grid compatibility remain unverified.

candidates.future_test_gate: Not viable until an exact official asset is obtained with a receipt and its license, coverage, bands, CRS and grid registration are verified. Only then, under renewed authorization, preregister the fixed halo and transforms, recompute with whole-segment hiding, and apply the canary and registry gates.
